To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) transient storage in Arctic streams is controlled by discharge and channel hydraulics (i.e., friction factor and unit stream power); (2) transient storage is not strongly related to permafrost thaw; and (3) the magnitude of transient storage in Arctic tundra channels is comparable to other streams in the literature.
